title: Every Grove Liquidity Layer interaction with an external protocol is gated on the RELAYER role before any other check
content:
The chunk repeats one clause verbatim for every externally callable operation: "The operator must ensure they are working as a `RELAYER`. Only the `RELAYER` role is allowed to..." — see A...7.2.1 (`withdrawAave`), A...8.1.1 (`swapCurve`), A...8.2.1 (`addLiquidityCurve`), A...8.3.1 (`removeLiquidityCurve`), A...9.1.1 (`swapUniswapV3`) and A...9.2.1 (`addLiquidityUniswapV3`).

In each case `_checkRole(RELAYER)` is the **first** statement of the function body, before index checks, slippage checks, or rate-limit accounting. Ordering matters: an unauthorised caller cannot use revert messages from the later validation stages to probe pool configuration, and the role check cannot be bypassed by any argument.

The design consequence is that Grove's safety story is two-layered rather than one. The RELAYER role answers *who* may move capital; the per-pool slippage and rate-limit configuration answers *how much* and *on what terms*. Compromising the relayer key does not grant unbounded access, because the second layer is enforced in the same transaction and is set by governance, not by the caller.

That also explains why the Atlas documents the role check as a distinct numbered step in every procedure instead of factoring it out: each function is specified as independently self-guarding, so no operation inherits its authorisation from a caller.
description: _checkRole(RELAYER) is the first statement of withdrawAave, swapCurve, addLiquidityCurve, removeLiquidityCurve, swapUniswapV3 and addLiquidityUniswapV3 — ahead of all parameter validation.
